title: Data Structure Supporting Median Deletion
statement_html:
Design a data structure that stores a multiset of integers and supports:

  • MedianDeleter() initializes an empty structure.

  • void add(int x) inserts the integer x.

  • int deleteMedian() removes the current median and returns it.

If the structure holds n elements, the median is the element of rank floor(n / 2) + 1 in ascending order, counting ranks from 1. For odd n it is the middle element; for even n it is the upper of the two middle elements.

Both operations should run in O(log n) time.

Example 1:

Input
["MedianDeleter","add","add","add","deleteMedian","add","add","deleteMedian","deleteMedian"]
[[],[5],[1],[3],[],[8],[2],[],[]]
Output
[null,null,null,null,3,null,null,5,2]
Explanation
add 5, 1, 3 -> {1,3,5}, n = 3, rank 2: deleteMedian() returns 3, leaving {1,5}
add 8, 2    -> {1,2,5,8}, n = 4, rank 3: deleteMedian() returns 5, leaving {1,2,8}
               n = 3, rank 2: deleteMedian() returns 2, leaving {1,8}

Example 2:

Input
["MedianDeleter","add","deleteMedian","add","add","deleteMedian"]
[[],[4],[],[7],[7],[]]
Output
[null,null,4,null,null,7]
Explanation: Duplicates are allowed; {7,7} has median 7.

Constraints:

  • -109 <= x <= 109

  • At most 105 calls in total

  • deleteMedian is only called when the structure is non-empty

Similar to LeetCode #295. Find Median from Data Stream (differs in: the median is removed, and it is always the single element of rank floor(n/2)+1).
